title: Your lottery ticket
hook: Does choosing a ticket change its odds or just the price you demand?

knows: basic arithmetic and reading a small table
doesNotKnow: Separate control over selection from control over a random outcome.

misconception: The quantities in this case can be combined without checking their reference, denominator, or information boundary.
objective: Separate control over selection from control over a random outcome.
keyState: Both complete computed cases are visible as retained observations; the question-case picture survives Reset.

claims.text: A toy lottery has ten equally likely tickets. Choosing your own ticket instead of receiving one changes its winning chance to what? Toy inputs A=[10, 1, 0]; B=[10, 0, 1].
claims.source: Local explicit hypothetical assumptions in spec.ts and model.ts; not participant measurements.

claims.text: Computed results: [[10, 1, 0], [10, 0, 1]]. Labels: Chance %, Self-picked, Assigned.
claims.source: compute() in the lesson-local model.ts; finite numeric operations over the explicit inputs.

claims.text: The rule assigns equal probability to every ticket. The selection method changes who chooses the label, not the draw distribution. Any ownership value or willingness to sell is a separate measured response.
claims.source: The two controlled cases in spec.ts; scope limited to these toy inputs and displayed model rule.

claims.text: A new toy case uses Equal tickets=10, Self-picked=0, Assigned=1. What is Chance %? Answer: 10.
claims.source: compute() applied to the contrasting new input case; source list is an idea pointer only.

recall.question: A new toy case uses Equal tickets=10, Self-picked=0, Assigned=1. What is Chance %?
recall.why: Applying the stated toy rule to the new inputs gives 10. The result depends on these assumptions; it is not a universal behavioral response.

sourceProvenance.text: Office workers who chose their own lottery ticket asked $8.67 to sell it, versus $1.96 for those assigned one (Langer, 1975).
sourceProvenance.caveat: Original list says figures are approximate and papers were not individually rechecked. No empirical source is verified by this build.

meaningfulDifference: Separate control over selection from control over a random outcome.
